title: Breathomics (Breath gas markers) for clinical states and NMDAR functioning in depression
summary:
One of the most common psychiatric disorders is depressive disorder with a lifetime prevalence of 15%. Depression can be effectively treated with psychotherapy and/or antidepressants that act on serotonergic, noradrenergic, and nowadays glutamatergic neurotransmission. However, one third of patients do not respond to 2 different antidepressants and need different treatment options as early as possible. 
Unfortunately, no objective measurement methods are currently available that could support diagnosis and also therapy finding. In a preliminary study we were able to identify some substances by measurements from the breath, which clearly differ between patients with depression and healthy subjects. However, the significance of these substances for brain function is currently unclear. 
The presented study intends to relate these substances from breath to known markers derived by electrophysiology (EEG) and 7 Tesla MRI spectroscopy.

interventions.name: 25 patients with a major depressive disorder will be investigated with 7 T MRI as well as EEG and evoked potentials. Moreover, psychopathology will be assessed and breath gas will be collected

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
depressive episode according to DSM V (major depressive disorder)
being able to understand the study procedure
Exclusion criteria:
- Exclusion criteria for the performance of an MRI examination
- Pregnancy in women
- current (present or in the last 4 weeks) treatment with an antidepressant drug
- depressive episode with psychotic symptoms
- acute suicidality, suicidal intent, or suicidal plans
- alcohol and/or drug dependence according to DSM-V 
- history of drug-induced psychosis
- organic diseases affecting brain function (hormonal diseases, e.g. thyroid disease) 
- subjects that cannot communicate during the MRI scanning via the speaker with the MR employees due to illness related disturbances or disturbances as side effects of medication
- infectious diseases, bronchial asthma, and other diseases affecting the pulmonary system
- current cancer (or in the last year)
- neurological diseases such as Parkinson's disease, stroke, multiple sclerosis
- diabetes mellitus
- comorbid axis I disease
- patients participating in another clinical investigation
